neighbours.label: a possessive determiner pointing back to a whole just before a noun for its inner part ('at their center', 'at its heart', 'the galaxies' cores'), as against the same sentence continuing without a part noun
fire: Most hurricanes form a calm eye at their center.
The old city still has a busy market at its heart.
The cells keep their genetic material in their nuclei.
The planets carry iron and nickel at their cores.
The village keeps a small chapel at its center.
The dancers reduced the steps to their simplest movements.
Most cherries hold a single hard stone at their middle.
Old trees can grow hollow at their hearts after many years.
quiet: Most hurricanes form a calm eye that moves slowly.
The old city still runs a busy market every Sunday.
The cells divide quickly in warm conditions.
The planets move slowly across the night sky.
The village keeps a small chapel near the river.
The dancers practised the steps every afternoon.
Most cherries ripen in the early part of summer.
Old trees can grow very tall after many years.
